surfaces.part: open ground-floor arcade with pillars, door and stalls

answer.evidence: The main body is a hall with a large sloped tile roof. The roof plane runs rows 15-45 (width grows from 62 to 128 px) and ends in a light edge line at rows 46-47, preceded by dark eave shadow at rows 43-45. Below it is a front face of about 48 rows: a timber-framed upper storey (rows 48-62), a beam, and an open arcade with posts, door and stalls (rows 63-95). The dormer has its own conical spire roof, which reads as a roof surface. The hip slopes at the left and right are part of the same roof plane, not a receding side wall.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's tile roof has several tone steps (highlight, light, mid, dark, deep) with per-tile scallops and speckle, matching the Beodeul roofs. Walls carry plaster speckle, timber beams and shaded stonework at the base, and the market goods and barrels are varied. Measured facts agree: 17 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 in the references, 1% near-flat coverage against 0%, and only 6% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outlines lean brown or red-brown rather than black. It reads as a dark material-tone outline, not a sticker look. Density is at or above the references, so this passes.
